questions.q: Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence.
questions.s:
Correct Answer:Brilliant

Explanation:
The sentence is:
"Navika is a superb and impressive child in her class."

We need a word that can replace "superb and impressive" and still retain the intended meaning — that Navika is outstanding in ability, intelligence, or performance.

  • Brilliant ✅ – means very intelligent, talented, or excellent (अत्यंत प्रतिभाशाली या उत्कृष्ट), which is the best fit here.

  • Splendid – means very beautiful or impressive (शानदार), but usually used for things, not commonly for a child’s quality.

  • Dazzling – means extremely bright or impressive (चकाचौंध करने वाला), more about appearance than ability.

  • Vivid – means bright or clearly detailed (तेज या स्पष्ट), usually used for colours or memories, not people.

✅ Correct sentence:
"Navika is a brilliant child in her class."

questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.
o: a college now
Ms. Malathi is
questions.s:
Answer: old much

Explanation:
The phrase "old much" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "too old" when expressing that someone’s age prevents them from doing something.

Correct sentence:
"Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now."

Other parts:

  • "Ms. Malathi is" – correct

  • "to join" – correct

  • "a college now" – correct

Hence, "old much" is the part containing the error.

(b) She looks sad (linking verb)

questions.q:
Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.45_30-Oct_Shift-1)
o: The company came up with a brilliant marketing strategy.
We came in the meeting room quietly.
She always comes down with a cold in winter.
He came across an interesting article while researching.
questions.s:
Answer:We came in the meeting room quietly.

Explanation:
The error lies in the incorrect use of the preposition "in". The correct preposition is "into", because we are referring to movement towards the inside of the meeting room.

  • "Come into" is used for entering a space.

  • "Come in" is often used when the person is already at the threshold or when giving permission, like "Come in!"

Correct sentence:
We came into the meeting room quietly.

All the other sentences are grammatically correct.
